newsitem.title: IRAN: No new post-election Iran foreign policy-Velayati.
newsitem.headline: No new post-election Iran foreign policy-Velayati.

text.p: Iran's foreign minister on Sunday said there would be no change in the Islamic republic's foreign policy principles after next Friday's presidential election and held out little hope for better relations with the West.

Ali Akbar Velayati, at a news conference in Tehran, said a German court which accused Iran's leaders of involvement in the assassination of three Kurdish dissidents and their translator in Berlin would have to "rectify" its mistake.
And he said U.S. foreign policy in the Middle East and wider region was a failure.
Velayati said a statement from the German federal prosecutor's office that it would not pursue an investigation into Iran's leaders was insufficient.
"This would show that the Germans have not corrected themselves as they needed to. What happened is that the court was not a legal procedure but something political...
"They have to correct their approach," he said, later adding: "The legal procedures of the Germans in their judicial procedures need to be rectified."
The court's verdict was to be rejected and needed to be corrected, Velayati said.

"We did not say the European ambassadors should not return," he said. "What has been mentioned has been the utterances of eminent leaders of the revolution that all ambassadors could return except for the ambassador from Germany."

The German court's verdict implicating Iran's Shi'ite Moslem leadership -- vehemently denied in Iran -- raised tempers and flared into a long-distance slanging match last month between Tehran and European capitals.
Velayati said there would be no change in the principles of Iran's foreign policy because these had been defined since the beginning of the revolution by the supreme leader.
"Therefore, there would be no changes in principles of foreign policy."

"As far as the United States is concerned, you can see that the position of the United States has not been changed. The foreign policy of the United States towards Iran has not been changed and they have the same attitude."

Velayati said U.S. foreign policy had failed and former Secretary of State Warren Christopher had been changed "and has been succeeded by the new one". He did not mention the name of Christopher's successor, Madeleine Albright.
Velayati told a U.S. reporter one of the main reasons for the change was very clear -- "the defeat of your (U.S.) foreign policy in the Middle East".
The new U.S. foreign minister was chanting the same slogans which used to be chanted by the old one, he said.
"We know that you (the United States) are now in deadlock. There is no clear horizon in the Middle East for U.S. foreign policy.
"In Lebanon, Syria and Palestine the question of the Middle East as a whole is a very complicated question and even your friends in the region are disappointed."

Velayati said U.S. sanctions aimed at isolating Iran had failed. American oil companies had participated in a recent gas and oil seminar in Isfahan in spite of many warnings from the U.S. administration and some senators "and that's the reality".
